summary: Sanders County Skookum Point ground-level log cabin, built 1929, abandoned 1942, still standing in the 1980s; FFLA lists it gone. No site-today source.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; firelookout.com says the cabin was still there in the 1980s
facts.agency: Lolo National Forest and Montana DNRC

events.note: firelookout.com describes a log cabin dated 1929
still there in the 1980s; the source gives only the decade

evidence.supports: log cabin dated 1929, abandoned 1942, still there in the 1980s
about 26 miles NNE of Thompson Falls
agencies Lolo National Forest and Montana DNRC

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA gone status and firelookout.com's note that the cabin was still there in the 1980s do not conflict: the cabin stood in the 1980s, and the list now records it as gone.

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse this with Skookum Butte, a different and still-standing lookout on the Missoula and Idaho line (FFLA row: US 172, MT 14). The Skookum Point history rests on one firelookout.com page; I found no separate history page for it (guessed montanalookouts.weebly.com URLs returned 404). The only staffing date is the 1942 abandonment. No source describes what remains at the site today or whether the public can reach it.
